song.title: Are You Gonna Go My Way

guitar.modelsText: Gibson Flying V / Vintage Fender Stratocaster
guitar.evidence: Lenny Kravitz is known for playing a range of vintage guitars including Gibson Flying V and Stratocasters; no single defining signature model.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with medium confidence.

tone.target: tight fuzzed hard-rock riff with bright upper mids
tone.profile: tight fuzzed hard-rock riff with bright upper mids
tone.summary: A tight signal chain utilizing Fuzz for grit, a Boost/OD for punch, and the UK 45 amp with a 4x12 cab to deliver bright, aggressive hard rock tones.
gearClues: wah only if used on lead
corrections: Remove chorus and delay as defaults

rig.name: Lenny Kravitz - Are You Gonna Go My Way - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and noise from high-gain fuzz circuits.
Provide the core fuzzed grit and aggressive texture required for the riff.
Add tight punch and upper-mid bite for palm-muted articulation.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD/Green OD to maintain maximum tightness without muddying the fuzz core.

alternatives.reason: A solid alternative for punch, but might introduce too much mid-range coloration.

blocks.purpose: Optional wah for lead lines (as per verdict), but kept inactive for the core riff.
blocks.gap: The V-Wah is a general purpose choice; no specific Kravitz tone required it, so it's optional/inactive.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall/Plexi family sound and provide necessary upper-mid bite.

alternatives.reason: Also suitable, but UK 45 is often cited for that specific bright hard rock edge.

blocks.purpose: Deliver the required aggressive hard rock tone and complement the UK 45 amp model.
Fine-tune the upper mids for maximum bite and punch without sounding scooped.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 allows for more precise mid-range sculpting than EQ 1, which is crucial for 'upper-mid bite'.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and glue the aggressive riff without sounding lush or wet.
blocks.gap: The verdict specified avoiding 'lush delay' and 'chorus', so Room is used minimally for ambience only.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for maximum punch and clarity.

proposals.reason: Enhance the aggressive, punchy hard rock feel of the riff.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and definition in the low end/mids.
